To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) Amoeba proteas ability to form pinocytic channels after pretreatment of the cells with either puromyocin, cyclohexymide or emetine is similar.
(1) Na+-induced channel formation in Amoeba requires the presence of Ca2+; and (2) Na+-inducers do not induce pinocytosis in Ca2+-deficiency, but do so in the presence of Ca+2.

the induction of pinocytic vesicles by cations is inhibited by starvation and inhibitors such as puromycin, emetine and cycloheximade, and that this inhibition can be relieved by adding Ca2+ to the inducing solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of starvation and inhibitors of cell-free protein synthesis on pinocytotic channel formation in Amoeba.
the effects of starvation, inhibitors of protein synthesis and a proteolytic agent on the formation of pinocytotic vesicles in Amoeba.
the role of protein synthesis in the formation of pinocytotic vesicles in the Amoeba proteas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ca2+-dependent step in the pinocytotic sequence of events in Amoeba is not a membrane potential change, but is related to a Ca2+-releasable component in the cell membrane.
the inhibition of Na+-stimulated pinocytosis is a direct result of the depletion of the membrane of Ca2+-binding proteins.

the effect of inhibitors on pinocytotic channel formation is due to the inhibition of protein synthesis and that the effect of starvation on the same process is not due to the inhibition or starvation of protein synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pinocytosis in Amoeba is regulated by the membrane potential and by the concentration of calcium ions in the medium.

the Ca2+-stimulated cation-induced channel formation is a process which involves the synthesis and/or activation of a protein(s) which is sensitive to starvation and inhibition of protein synthesis and that this process is not related to the depolarising effect of the inducer on the cell membrane potential.

the induction of pinocytic channels in Amoeba by Na+ is Ca2+-dependent and that the Ca2+ requirement is mediated by a membrane structure which is depleted in starved cells and after inhibition of protein synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the induction of pinocytic channels by cationic stimuli is not a passive process.

the inhibition of protein synthesis in starved cells is not due to a general inhibition of the cell's metabolism, but is a specific phenomenon which is selective for Na+-like inducer-induced pinocytotic channel formation.
the effect of starvation, inhibitors of protein synthesis and enzyme digestion on pinocytotic channel formation is due to depletion of a Ca2+-dependent component of the membrane.
